text:
A: Hiya, you alright? I'm Joel, I'm in Manchester.
B: Hiya! I'm Gemma, I'm in Beeston, near Nottingham. Oh, your spare room's like ours, I said that when I saw the photo, with the airer.
A: (laughs) Yeah, it's half office, half drying rack, half bike storage. That's three halves, but it's a small room.
B: Honestly, same. So what do you do?
A: I'm a solicitor, corporate. So it's mainly business sales, share purchases, that sort of thing. Lots of owner-managed companies, people selling a firm they've built up over thirty years and they're dead nervous about it, so a lot of the job is sort of hand-holding, you know.
B: Oh, I bet. That's quite a big deal for people, isn't it.
A: It is, yeah. Had a completion run till midnight on Tuesday, so I'm still a bit knackered. What about you?
B: I'm a physio. MSK, NHS outpatients in Nottingham, and I do sports massage privately on Saturdays.
A: No way. My girlfriend's an MSK physio. Hannah. She's NHS as well, in Manchester.
B: Shut up! Is she? Okay, so she'll know all about the waiting list from hell then.
A: Oh, she talks about the waiting list like it's a person. Like it's moved in with us.
B: (laughs) It basically has. Ten-hour clinic day yesterday. I got home and just lay on the floor with the dog. Is she thinking of staying NHS? Because I'll be honest, I want to go for a Band 7, extended scope, and then longer term I'd love my own clinic, private physio and Pilates, do you know what I mean? Nice fit-out, be my own boss.
A: That's sort of what she talks about, actually, going private eventually. Do you think it's realistic? Sorry, that's the lawyer in me asking.
B: Erm, I think so? You need the clients first, which is why I do the Saturdays. Building it up, sort of thing.
A: Makes sense, yeah. If you ever do it, set it up properly, get a decent shareholder agreement if there's a business partner. Free advice, that, don't tell my firm.
B: (laughs) I'll hold you to that. You've got a dog in your photo? No, wait, that was someone else.
A: No dog yet. Hannah wants one, I'm slowly giving in. I reckon by Christmas.
B: Get a cockapoo. Mine's called Biscuit. Actually, I just spoke to a fella from Warrington with a cockapoo called Biscuit as well, it was mad.
A: Warrington? I'm from Warrington! Great Sankey. Was he a Wolves fan?
B: Yes! He had a magnet on the fridge.
A: Made up. There's a lot of us about. That'll have been him with the Wolves magnet, I spotted that in the photos.
B: Small world. And I grew up in Derby, so I'm a Rams fan, loosely, more for the day out than the football.
A: That's the right way to do it, to be fair. I'm Liverpool for football, which gets me some stick in Manchester, so I'm not one to judge.
